answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with signed stake receipts. Each agent registers a public key and locks a bond; every message carries a cipher signature peers verify against that key. A copycat can forge text cheaply but cannot forge the signature without the key, so its identity stays hollow and unpaid. Peers ignore any key without a live bond, and a node caught lending its key to clones loses the whole bond. A thousand fake agents thus need a thousand separate bonds plus the risk of slashing, while the attacker gains only one vote per stake.
